claim: Driving from Nerano/Marina del Cantone to Positano is roughly 16 miles and about 36 minutes in normal conditions.
quote: The driving distance between Nerano del Cantone to Positano is 16 miles... It takes approximately 36 min to drive from Nerano del Cantone to Positano.

claim: Nerano to Amalfi is around 24 miles and approximately 49 minutes by car under normal traffic.
quote: The driving distance between Nerano to Amalfi is 24 miles, and it takes approximately 49 minutes to drive from Nerano to Amalfi.

claim: Ravello sits about 29 miles and roughly 1 hour from Marina del Cantone by road.
quote: The driving distance between Ravello to Marina del Cantone is 29 miles, and it takes approximately 1 hour 1 minute to drive from Ravello to Marina del Cantone.

claim: Positano's town-centre ZTL operates 6:30am to midnight in summer with a directional switch at Mulini (descending 8:00-15:30, ascending 15:30-22:00), and only residents, taxis with bookings and licensed NCC drivers may enter; fines start around €145-150.
quote: Positano... ZTL Hours: '6:30am and midnight' during summer (approximately late June through mid-September), with a directional switching system at Mulini: descending 8:00-15:30, ascending 15:30-22:00... €145 commonly issued at Mulini camera.

claim: An alternate license-plate rule applies on the Amalfi Coast in summer 2026 — only even-plate cars may circulate on even-numbered days and only odd-plate cars on odd-numbered days; scooters are exempt and ZTL fines start above €80.
quote: Even-numbered days: Only cars with license plates ending in an even number can circulate. Odd-numbered days: Only cars with license plates ending in an odd number can circulate... Entering a ZTL zone without a permit results in an automatic fine of over €80.

claim: SITA Sud route 5070 (Sorrento-Positano-Amalfi) takes 90-100 minutes in normal conditions and stretches to 2-2.5 hours in July-August, and tickets cannot be bought on board — a 24-hour COSTIERASITA pass is €10.
quote: In normal conditions, the journey from Sorrento to Amalfi takes 90–100 minutes, though in summer (July–August) it can stretch to 2–2.5 hours due to traffic on the SS163... Tickets CANNOT be purchased on board the bus. A 24-hour COSTIERASITA ticket costs EUR 10.

claim: Returning SITA buses from Positano to Sorrento in summer often arrive already full from Amalfi, leaving intermediate-stop passengers stranded — so depart Positano well before peak return.
quote: during the busy summer months, it can be difficult to board the bus in Positano to return to Sorrento, as the buses often depart from Amalfi already at capacity so there is no room for additional passengers waiting at intermediate stops.

claim: Positano street parking runs about €3/hour with weekend summer spots near-impossible to find, while private garages can exceed €80/day, making a pre-booked garage essential for any car-based day trip.
quote: Parking in municipal spaces comes at a cost of 3€/h, in summer on weekends it is almost impossible to find parking... A garage can easily cost upward of €80 per day.

claim: Positano's signature sight is the Chiesa di Santa Maria Assunta, whose yellow-green-blue majolica-tiled dome defines the town skyline and houses a 13th-century Black Madonna Byzantine icon over Roman villa ruins.
quote: A central dome clad in yellow, green and blue majolica tiles makes the church one of Positano's distinctive landmarks... Inside the church, there is a 13th century Byzantine icon of the Black Madonna and child.

claim: Spiaggia Grande is Positano's iconic main beach and a top sunset spot, best paired with a walk along the cliffside Via Positanesi d'America to Fornillo beach.
quote: The Spiaggia Grande is the most famous beach of Positano, an iconic place from which you can enjoy a breathless view overlooking the small town. Spiaggia Grande is a favorite place to watch sunset on the Amalfi Coast.

claim: Praiano's must-dos are sunset at Cala della Gavitella (the only Amalfi Coast cove that watches the sun set straight into the sea, reached by 400+ steps from Piazza San Gennaro), the majolica-domed Church of San Gennaro, and the start of the Path of the Gods toward Bomerano.
quote: Cala della Gavitella, a small paradise nestled between the cliffs... is the only place on the Amalfi Coast where the sun appears to dive directly into the sea. It can be reached either by sea or via a scenic staircase of over 400 steps starting from Piazza San Gennaro.

claim: Amalfi's headline sight is the Duomo di Sant'Andrea atop its grand staircase on Piazza Duomo, with the Cloister of Paradise, the crypt holding St Andrew's relics, and a basilica blending Byzantine-Gothic-Baroque elements.
quote: The majestic Amalfi Cathedral, officially known as the Duomo di Sant'Andrea, stands proudly at the top of a grand staircase... The crypt where the relics of Saint Andrew are kept... The Chiostro del Paradiso, or Cloister of Paradise.

claim: Amalfi's Paper Museum sits in a 13th-century mill in the Valle dei Mulini, a 15-minute walk inland from Piazza Duomo, with working ancient machinery and live demonstrations of single-sheet paper production.
quote: The museum is housed within a 13th-century paper mill—one of the oldest and best-preserved in Europe. Located in the atmospheric Valle dei Mulini (Valley of the Mills), just a 15-minute walk from Piazza Duomo.

claim: Villa Cimbrone's gardens — anchored by the Terrace of Infinity — open daily from 9:00 until one hour before sunset, and the most-recommended visit windows are 9am opening or late afternoon to avoid heat and crowds.
quote: The gardens are open from 9:00 AM until one hour after sunset, which is 7:30 PM in summer and 5:30 PM in winter... Be there at 9am to avoid the crowds.

claim: Villa Rufolo on Ravello's main piazza pairs Moorish arches and tiered sea-facing gardens with Wagner associations, and tickets should be booked ahead in high season.
quote: Villa Rufolo is centrally located and features Moorish arches, lush gardens, and balconies overlooking the sea and Ravello's main piazza. Composer Richard Wagner visited the villa in 1880 and was so inspired by its beauty that he used it as inspiration for the garden of Klingsor in his opera Parsifal.

claim: Ravello's historic centre is a permanent 24/7 ZTL — cars stop at the town entrance and walk in, with the main public garages at Piazza del Duomo and Via della Repubblica.
quote: Entire historic centre is a permanent ZTL... Only residents, authorized suppliers, and licensed vehicles permitted. Visitors park at town entrance and walk.

claim: Cooperativa Sant'Antonio runs daily shared 8-hour boat tours from Nerano to Capri and to the Amalfi Coast from €60 per person, with morning departures and onboard guide.
quote: Capri Shared Tour ... FROM 60 € PER PERSON ... Duration: 8 hours ... Amalfi Coast Shared Tour ... Morning departure: 9:00 AM ... Late-morning departure: 11:15 AM

claim: Coop Sant'Antonio is the #1-rated boat operator in Nerano (4.7/5, 915 reviews) with private Capri tours reported at around €124 per person in August 2025; captains add bruschetta and Aperol Spritz on board.
quote: ranked #1 of 7 outdoor activities in Nerano ... 4.7 out of 5 ... One August 2025 reviewer reported paying €124 per person ... captain made us delicious home made bruschetta and Aperol Spritz

claim: There is no scheduled ferry from Marina del Cantone to Capri; reaching Capri publicly requires bus to Sorrento and then a fast ferry, otherwise a private charter from Nerano.
quote: There is no direct connection from Marina del Cantone to Capri. However, you can take the line 007 bus to Massa Lubrense ... take the bus to Sorrento, walk to Port Of Sorrento, then take the ferry to Port of Capri

claim: Blue Grotto admission in 2026 is €18 plus €12 for the rowboat, accessed only from Marina Grande or land via Anacapri; swimming inside is prohibited and the cave closes in rough seas.
quote: €18 per person for grotto admission (plus €12 for the rowboat) ... Swimming is prohibited ... the cave closes during rough seas or high winds

claim: Capri's 2026 overtourism rules cap tour groups at 40 people, ban loudspeakers and raised umbrellas/flags, and signal future restrictions on Marina Grande boat traffic — but no hard daily visitor cap.
quote: Tour groups are limited to a maximum of 40 people ... Loudspeakers are forbidden ... Mayor Paolo Falco indicated plans to restrict boat traffic at Marina Grande port

claim: Capri raised its accommodation levy from January 2026 and is collecting more day-tripper tax through ferry ticket pricing, with restaurant-touts fines near €700 — but no Venice-style turnstile.
quote: slightly higher nightly charges on the island from January 2026 ... day-trippers may see ticket prices for ferries ... adjusted to reflect local landing and port fees ... fines approaching 700 euros

claim: FAI's Baia di Ieranto is open free dawn-to-dusk via a 2.5 km / 50-minute trail from Nerano; private motorboats and beach landings are forbidden, kayaking only via guided activity.
quote: open to the public every day, from dawn until one hour before sunset ... Private motorized boats are prohibited in the protected marine area ... Beach landings are forbidden ... Kayaking is available through specialist-led activities

claim: Ieranto Bay sits inside the Punta Campanella Marine Protected Area directly opposite Capri and is guarded by two Saracen towers; only authorised charter operators can enter the top-protection zone.
quote: Ieranto Bay is a marine protected natural reserve, a pristine inlet located directly across from Capri and guarded by two Saracen Towers ... authorized charter operators can access even the areas with the top degree of protection like Ieranto Bay

claim: Masticiello Boat Service in Marina del Cantone rents Gozzi Sorrentini 6–10 m, speedboats and inflatables with or without skipper for day trips to Capri's Faraglioni, Blue Grotto, Positano and Amalfi.
quote: Gozzi Sorrentini from 6 to 10 meters with or without driver, speedboats up to 6 meters with outboard motors ... luxury day charters to Capri, its Faraglioni and the Blue Grotto

claim: Luxury Boats Positano's 7-hour Li Galli & Nerano private voyage starts at €1,500 for up to 12 guests and pairs Sirens-island swimming with a Marina del Cantone lunch and Crapolla Cove inside the Punta Campanella MPA.
quote: Price: From €1,500 ... Duration: 7 hours ... Up to 12 people ... Li Galli Islands: Swimming in waters associated with Homer's Odyssey sirens legend ... Crapolla Cove: Exploration of hidden grottos in the Marine Protected Area of Punta Campanella

claim: Capri.com lists a Private Capri Boat Tour with Lunch Stop in Nerano at €600 for 2026, with a Conca del Sogno variant at €700 and Gozzo Sorrentino charters in the €550–€1,020 range.
quote: Private Capri Boat Tour with Lunch Stop in Nerano ... €600.00 ... Boat Tour of Capri with a Stop at La Conca Del Sogno is priced at €700.00 ... Gozzo Sorrentino with Ciro Capri Boats: €550 ... Capasecca Yacht: €1,020

claim: Massa Lubrense town centre clusters around Santa Maria delle Grazie church with a panoramic terrace, and roads branch out to Sant'Agata, Marciano and Nerano beaches; a car or scooter is essential to get around.
quote: just a few steps from the panoramic terrace overlooking the sea... one leads to the hills of Sant'Agata sui due Golfi and the other to Marciano, the Nerano beaches... you must have a car or scooter to get around.

claim: Marina della Lobra is a small fishing harbour below Massa Lubrense town, about 6 km by SS145 from Sorrento, reachable by SITA bus to Massa then walk/taxi down a winding road.
quote: By road, it is around 6 kilometers away, following the SS145 coastal road towards Massa Lubrense. From there, a winding local road leads down to the marina. Local SITA buses run from Sorrento to Massa Lubrense, where visitors can either walk or take a taxi to Marina della Lobra.

claim: Above Marina della Lobra sits the 16th-century church of Santa Maria della Lobra built over a Roman church, with a 17th-century ceiling, cloisters and 18th-century majolica floor; the village is inside the Punta Campanella Marine Protected Area and holds a Bandiera Blu.
quote: Just above the marina is a 16th century church, Santa Maria della Lobra, which was built over a Roman church. It has a 17th century ceiling and cloisters while the majolica floor is 18th century.

claim: The Punta Campanella walking path starts in Termini hamlet, last village on the western tip of the peninsula, and is reachable by SITA bus 20-30 min from Sorrento; the trail is 4 km / 2 hours round-trip and easy.
quote: Termini is readily accessible by the 10.30 Sita bus from Sorrento... From the little square of Termini, piazza Santa Croce, head down via Campanella, then after about 200 metres take the first turning to the right in the direction of via Minerva, a Greek-Roman mule track built in the fourth century B.C.

claim: Punta Campanella tip holds the remains of a 14th-century Saracen watchtower on the former site of a temple of Athena, with celebrated views across to Capri.
quote: you can visit the remains of a Saracen tower built in the 1300s on the spot where there was once a statue of the goddess Athena

claim: Sant'Agata sui Due Golfi is a small hilltop village famed for the marble-and-lapis-lazuli altar of Santa Maria delle Grazie, the 17th-century belvedere of the Monastero del Deserto, and it is the home of Don Alfonso 1890.
quote: There's a church in the main square – Santa Maria delle Grazie – which has a famous marble alter decorated with shiny mother of pearl and lapis lazuli stone. You can climb to the Monastery of San Paolo's tower, or 'belvedere', which looks out to the Amalfi Coast, and it dates back to the 1600s.

claim: Sant'Agata is the gastronomic anchor of the peninsula thanks to chef Alfonso Iaccarino and his two-Michelin-starred Don Alfonso 1890.
quote: This is where the great chef Alfonso Iaccarino and his Michelin-starred "Don Alfonso 1890" reigns supreme.

claim: Pizza a Metro 'Da Gigino' in Vico Equense is the original 1930s home of pizza-by-the-meter, in the town centre at Corso Nicotera 15.
quote: Pizza a Metro da Gigino is the historic restaurant pizzeria founded by Gigino Dell'Amura where, back in the 1930s, the "pizza by the meter" was born.

claim: Vico Equense's Castello Giusso, built 1284 as a coastal defence, was converted into a noble palace and now hosts cultural events with cliff-top terraces over the Bay of Naples.
quote: Castello Giusso was built in 1284 as a defensive structure with military quarters and supply storage. The ancient military structures were destroyed to make room for a residential palace commissioned by Ferrante Carafa, which today features cliff-top terraces overlooking the sea

claim: Vico Equense pairs the Scrajo thermal baths, the Marina di Vico beach and the cliff-side Annunziata church with hiking access to Monte Faito and the Path of the Gods.
quote: The Scrajo Terme offer thermal spring experiences for relaxation and regeneration, while the Marina di Vico beach is ideal for sun and sea. Hiking enthusiasts can venture onto Monte Faito or along the famous Path of the Gods.

claim: A half-day in Sorrento itself centres on Piazza Tasso, the cliff-top Villa Comunale park with views to Vesuvius and Capri, and the historic Sedile Dominova noble loggia on Via San Cesareo.
quote: Villa Comunale is one of Sorrento's most beautiful public parks that offers breathtaking views of the Bay of Naples, Mount Vesuvius, and the island of Capri in the distance.

claim: The 14th-century Sedile Dominova, with open loggia, majolica-tiled dome and 18th-century frescoes, is one of the few surviving Italian noble-seat halls.
quote: this elegant structure dates back to the 14th century and once served as a gathering place for the town's aristocracy, who met here to discuss political and civic matters. The building remains remarkably intact, with an open loggia supported by stone columns and crowned by a striking tiled dome in yellow and green majolica.

claim: Recommone bay sits a short walk (about 10 minutes) east of Marina del Cantone in Nerano, home to the Conca del Sogno hotel-restaurant-beach club.
quote: From Marina del Cantone a short, 10 minute walk leads to Recommone bay... On the far side of the bay is the idyllic hotel-restaurant-beach club La Conca del Sogno.

claim: Recommone is a sheltered bay with two sea caves (Grotta di Recommone, Grotta dei Pescatori) and the Conca del Sogno bathing establishment.
quote: the bay also has two caves: the Grotta di Recommone and the Grotta dei Pescatori, both of which offer holidaymakers a wonderfully cool refuge in the hottest hours of the day.

claim: FAI Baia di Ieranto seasonal schedule: Tuesday-Sunday March 1 – October 31; weekends only January, February, November, December; access is by foot only from Nerano, private motorboats prohibited.
quote: March 1 - October 31: Tuesday-Sunday. November & December: Saturday-Sunday only. percorrenza circa 45 minuti. dislivelli di circa 250 mt. Access is by foot only from Nerano; private motorboats are prohibited.

claim: Bay of Ieranto access is via the municipal trail from Nerano square; private motorboats and beach landings are forbidden and a Castellammare di Stabia Harbour Master ordinance temporarily restricts swimming in certain marine areas.
quote: Private motorized boats are prohibited, as well as landing on the beach in this marine area. All visitors are requested to carefully read the ordinance issued by the Harbour Master's Office of Castellammare di Stabia regarding the marine areas temporarily closed to swimming in the Baia di Ieranto.

claim: Ieranto round-trip is roughly 6 km / 3 hours; visitors are advised to time the climb back up for late afternoon to avoid peak sun.
quote: 6 km round-trip. 3 hours (round trip). plan to climb back up in late afternoon, when the sun is not at its hottest.

claim: Path of the Gods Bomerano→Nocelle is 5.6 km, 215 m ascent / 410 m descent, 1.5–3 hours, easy-to-moderate, best done in this direction (mostly downhill); spring through early June and late September through November are ideal, summer is hot and crowded, much of trail is shadeless so carry 1.5 L water per person.
quote: Length: 5.6 km (3.5 miles) from Bomerano to Nocelle. Elevation gain: 215 m (710 ft); loss: 410 m (1,345 ft). Duration: 1.5–3 hours. Spring (April through early June) and the fall (end of September through November) offer ideal conditions. at least 1.5 liters of water per person.

claim: Path of the Gods is one of AllTrails' top-reviewed Campania trails, with the Nocelle–Bomerano direction alone showing 1,431 reviews.
quote: Path of the Gods: Nocelle - Bomerano, Campania, Italy - 1,431 Reviews

claim: Punta Campanella from Termini is ~7.1 km return, 600 m elevation gain, moderate, 3–4 hours along the ancient Roman Via Minerva with views of Capri, the Temple of Minerva ruins and a medieval watchtower next to the lighthouse.
quote: Distance: 7.1 km (return). Elevation Gain: 600 m. Difficulty: Moderate. Duration: 3-4 hours. Trailhead Location: Santa Croce Square in Termini. the remains of a medieval watchtower with a modern lighthouse beside it.

claim: AllTrails lists a Punta Campanella via Nerano – Punta Penna loop at 7.7 miles (~12.4 km) with 2,677 ft (~816 m) elevation gain — useful if combining Ieranto with Punta Campanella as a single big day.
quote: This is a 7.7-mile loop trail near Massa Lubrense, Campania, and it has an elevation gain of 2,677 ft.

claim: Monte San Costanzo (485 m summit) is reached from Termini's Piazza Santa Croce via Via Campanella and the ancient Via Minerva; not an easy excursion, requires basic athletic training and trekking shoes, with 360° views over the Gulfs of Naples and Salerno plus Capri, Ischia and Procida.
quote: The walking path begins in Termini, the last hamlet on the western coast of the Sorrentine Peninsula. take Via Campanella for about 400 meters. not an easy excursion. you'll see the Gulf of Naples, the Gulf of Salerno and the suggestive chain of the Lattari Mountains.

claim: The Punta Campanella – Monte Santa Croce loop via Termini is 5.6 miles (~9 km) with 1,794 ft (~547 m) elevation gain, 3.5–4 hours, combining Monte San Costanzo's neighbouring summit with the cape.
quote: Punta Campanella - Monte Santa Croce via Termini... This is a loop trail that covers 5.6 miles with an elevation gain of 1,794 ft, and it takes about 3.5–4 hours to complete.

claim: The Pimonte/Gragnano Valle dei Mulini trail leaves Piazza Aubry, traces the mill valley to the Forma spring and climbs to Castello hamlet before joining the Monti Lattari high road; well-marked to the Church of Pino, but the upper section is poorly marked and a GPS track is recommended.
quote: starts from Piazza Aubry (the conceria), runs entirely through the Valle dei Mulini di Gragnano to the source of Forma and rises to the Castello fraction... from the Church of Pino to the end of the trail it is not very well-marked and it's recommended to have a digital trace and GPS.

claim: The neighbouring Valle delle Ferriere via Valle dei Mulini loop above Amalfi is 3.2 miles (~5.1 km) with ~925 ft (~282 m) gain, 2–2.5 hours, moderate, with waterfalls and lemon orchards.
quote: A moderate hike through the Valle delle Ferriere via Valle dei Mulini covers 3.2 miles with an elevation gain of 925 feet and takes about 2–2.5 hours to complete. Reviewers highlight stunning views of the Mediterranean, waterfalls, and lovely lemon orchards.

claim: The wider Sorrentine peninsula trail network includes Monte Faito (reached by cable car from Castellammare di Stabia), the Path of the Gods, the Punta Campanella cobblestoned Minerva road, and the Ieranto Bay marine reserve walk — the four canonical options for a Nerano-based hiker.
quote: Punta Campanella Trail: cobblestoned paved path dating back to ancient Romans, following the old Minerva road. Path of the Gods: stunning views throughout the approximately 5km hike from Bomerano to Nocelle. Monte Faito: cable car from Castellammare di Stabia. Ieranto Bay: A walking route within the Marine Natural Reserve of Punta Campanella.

claim: Pompeii 2026 ticket categories: Pompeii Only €20, Pompeii Plus (incl. Oplontis & Stabiae) €30, Pompeii Express not listed in update; annual MyPompeii Card €45.
quote: Pompeii + Suburban Villas + Boscoreale: €25.00; Pompeii Only: €20.00; Pompeii Plus (includes Oplontis, Stabiae sites): €30.00; Annual Pass (MyPompeii): €45.00

claim: From 2 March 2026, Pompeii tickets are sold exclusively through vivaticket.com, replacing TicketOne as the official partner.
quote: From 2 March 2026, tickets are sold exclusively through vivaticket.com — which replaced TicketOne as the official ticketing partner.

claim: Herculaneum 2026 standard adult ticket is €16; reduced €2 for EU 18-25; annual pass €30 (family €58, youth €5).
quote: Standard admission: €16; Reduced ticket: €2; Young adults (18-25): €2. Individual annual pass: €30; Family pass (2 adults + children): €58; Youth annual pass (18-25): €5

claim: Mount Vesuvius online booking is compulsory; entry is staggered in 60-person groups every 10 minutes, with a 40-minute grace before and 120-minute window after the booked slot.
quote: Entry is staggered, group of 60 people every 10 minutes, so booking is compulsory … a grace period of 40 minutes before and 120 minutes after

claim: Vesuvius National Park standard entry to hike Gran Cono trail to the crater is €10.
quote: General admission to the Vesuvius National Park costs €10, which allows you to hike the Gran Cono Trail

claim: Villa A (Villa of Poppaea) at Oplontis costs €5; entry is also free with a valid Pompeii ticket used within 30 days.
quote: The ticket for Villa A (The Villa of Poppaea) costs €5.00. Additionally, entry is free with a valid Pompeii ticket within 30 days of issue.

claim: Stabia's Villa San Marco and Villa Arianna are free of charge; open daily 9:00-18:00 except Tuesdays; visit takes ~2 hours.
quote: The archaeological site is open daily from 9 am to 6 pm, except on Tuesdays. There is no entrance fee to the Stabia villas.

claim: Driving from Nerano to Pompeii is 36.3 km, taking ~51 minutes by the A3 route.
quote: Distance: 36.3 km by road; Duration: 51 min of driving time; Estimated Cost: €6–9

claim: Driving from Herculaneum to Nerano takes around 1 hour 4 minutes.
quote: You can drive from Herculaneum to Nerano in around 1 hour 4 minutes.

claim: Pompeii is reached via the A3 motorway 'Pompei Ovest' exit leading directly to the archaeological park; multiple paid lots near the entrance (e.g. Parking Zeus Area 2, 70 m from Porta Marina Superiore).
quote: The highway A3 Pompei Ovest exit leads directly to the archaeological park entrance … Parking Zeus Area 2 is located just 70 meters away from the Porta Marina Superiore entrance

claim: The Villa of the Mysteries holds the most extraordinary cycle of ancient wall paintings — 29 near-life-size figures on Pompeian-red ground depicting a Dionysiac initiation, plus an original wine torcularium.
quote: The Villa of the Mysteries contains the most extraordinary cycle of ancient wall paintings in existence — 29 near-life-size figures on a deep Pompeian red background depicting a Dionysiac initiation rite.

claim: The House of the Faun is Pompeii's largest private house (>3,000 m²), famous for the bronze dancing faun and the Alexander Mosaic depicting the Battle of Issus.
quote: Covering over 3,000 square meters, it is one of the largest and most opulent residences unearthed in the ancient city … the Alexander Mosaic, depicting the Battle of Issus

claim: Herculaneum's Casa di Nettuno e Anfitrite preserves a brilliantly coloured wall mosaic of Neptune and a nymph, and is one of the site's most visited houses.
quote: The dining area is decorated with beautiful wall mosaics including a famous image of Neptune and a nymph.

claim: Herculaneum boathouses contain around 300 skeletons of victims who sheltered there awaiting rescue boats and died from the pyroclastic surge (~500°C).
quote: In the 1980s, excavations of the area around the ancient port discovered the remains of around 300 people … They died due to a sudden increase in temperature upwards of 500 degrees Celsius.

claim: Tenuta Vannulo (Capaccio Paestum) is the famous organic buffalo mozzarella estate; bookings via info@vannulo.it or +39 0828 727 894; dairy open Mon-Sun 8:00-17:00 with tasting room 12:00-16:00.
quote: Via Galileo Galilei, 101, Contrada Vannulo, 84047 Capaccio Paestum-SA, Italy ... Dairy: Mon-Sun, 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM ... Tasting Room: Mon-Sun, 12:00 PM – 4:00 PM

claim: Vannulo guided farm tours in Italian, English or French last 50 minutes, cost €40 per group (max 10), should be booked 2-3 days ahead and run through the cheese-processing area, stable, agricultural museum and mozzarella tasting; fresh mozzarella usually sells out by early afternoon.
quote: Guided tours in Italian, English or French last 50 minutes and cost €40 per group, to be divided according to number of participants (max. 10) ... visits proceed through the cheese-processing area, stable, agricultural museum and culminate in that all-important mozzarella tasting

claim: Cantina del Vesuvio (Russo family, Trecase) offers a 1.5-2 hour wine-tasting-with-lunch in the cellar at €50 classic / €60 superior — guided vineyard/cellar tour, 5 wines and a 3-course lunch — plus a €185 private 4-course lunch at the family villa accompanied by the winemaker; shuttle from Pompeii Porta Marina or Torre Annunziata available.
quote: Price: €50 (classic) or €60 (superior) per person ... Sampling of 5 wines ... 3-course lunch ... Wine Tasting with Private Lunch at the Villa Price: €185 per person ... shuttle service available from Pompeii Porta Marina and Torre Annunziata stations

claim: Cantina del Vesuvio takes reservations through Tock and confirms €50 Classico / €63 Superior wine-tasting-with-lunch pricing in 2026, with vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options and reduced €25 children's lunch.
quote: The 'Classico' Wine Tasting with Lunch is €50.00 per person, while the 'Superior' Wine Tasting with Lunch is €63.00 per person ... Children under 4 are free, and children between 4 and 18 can enjoy lunch without wine for EUR 25

claim: Sorrentino Vini in Boscotrecase (Via Panoramica 2) is a 300-year-old, five-generation Lacryma Christi producer; their winery-tasting experiences average around €65 (range €30-€100), bookable online, and the estate is not on public transport so the winery can arrange a taxi.
quote: Sorrentino winery was established 300 years ago in Boscotrecase and has been producing the legendary Lacryma Christi wine for five generations ... average price of a wine tasting with winery visit in Vesuvius is around €65 ... The winery cannot be reached by public transport, but Sorrentino Vini can arrange a taxi

claim: La Limonaia Sorrento runs a ~45-minute guided IGP-lemon-grove tour at €35 pp (group rate) — €65 with lunch — covering cultivation of the Ovale lemon and tastings of limoncello, marmalades, provolone del Monaco, lemon olive oil, honey and lemon biscuits, at Via Bernardino Rota 4 in central Sorrento.
quote: Duration: Approximately 45 minutes ... Standard tour: €35 per person (group rates) ... Tour with lunch/dinner: From €65 per person ... tastings of limoncello, limoncello cream, marmalades, provolone del Monaco cheese, lemon/orange olive oil, honey and lemon biscuits ... Via Bernardino Rota, 4 80067 Sorrento

claim: A Massa Lubrense lemon discovery tour (close to Nerano) claims to be the only one in Campania to follow the entire production cycle of a Sorrento lemon plant from grafting, with panoramic views over Ischia, Procida and the Gulf of Naples.
quote: the only one in the entire Campania region to follow the entire production process of a lemon plant in the most ancient and traditional way ... you can see where the lemon is born, the islands of Ischia and Procida, the Gulf of Naples

claim: Limonoro in central Sorrento offers a free walk-in limoncello, meloncello and confectionery tasting with staff explaining each product, with no obligation to buy.
quote: As soon as you walk in, you are greeted by staff with a variety of lemon-cello drinks and foods ... You are not obliged to purchase anything; you can visit just to enjoy the tasting experience

claim: Mamma Agata in Ravello (Piazza San Cosma 9) runs a single-sitting cooking class starting 10:00 with lemon cake, a 3-hour cook-along of eggplant parmigiana, spaghetti, chicken with lemon and zucchini-flower pizzelle, then lunch on the terrace 14:00-16:30; reviewers consistently advise booking 3-6 months ahead.
quote: begins at 10:30, where you are welcomed by Chiara, Mamma Agata's daughter ... eggplant parmigiana, spaghetti of the farmer, chicken with lemon, and zucchini flower pizzelle ... booking 3-6 months ahead to secure a spot

claim: L'Antica Pizzeria da Michele in Naples serves only Margherita and Marinara at €6 each; the dine-in storefront sits opposite a takeaway, and the queue trick is to go to the entrance and ask for a number rather than join the takeaway line, with pizzas served 5-10 minutes after seating.
quote: Each pizza costs €6 ... Go straight to the entrance and ask for a number. Do not wait in the takeaway line if you want to dine in ... Pizzas are served within 5-10 minutes

claim: Gino Sorbillo on Via dei Tribunali 32, Naples, is a Michelin Guide-listed Neapolitan pizzeria headed by a third-generation pizzaiolo, praised for fresh ingredients and authentic dough.
quote: Gino Sorbillo, a third-generation pizza maker, has earned accolades from prestigious guides like Michelin ... His flagship pizzeria on Via dei Tribunali has been mentioned in the prestigious Michelin Guide

claim: Naples pizzerias typically close 15:00-18:00/19:00, so day-trippers should plan an 11:00 arrival at Da Michele or visit Sorbillo on Via Tribunali 32 for the liveliest atmosphere; the Circumvesuviana from Sorrento is the standard rail link.
quote: Pizzerias in Naples close at 3pm and reopen at around 6-7pm ... plan on being there no later than 11:00 AM at Da Michele ... The Sorbillo location offers the liveliest, most atmospheric experience ... The Circumvesuviana is the train line that connects Naples to a string of villages along the bay, including Pompeii and Sorrento
